question.problem: Which root(s) of the polynomial $p(x)=2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+32x+16$ have multiplicity $2?$
question.worked_solution:
We factor the cubic by grouping, and simplify until the polynomial is fully factored:

$$
\begin{aligned}p(x) & =2{x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+32x+16 \\  & ={x}^{2}(2x+1)+16(2x+1) \\  & =({x}^{2}+16)(2x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Note that the factor $({x}^{2}+16)$ cannot be factored any further, and it does not have any real roots.

The only real root of $p(x)$ comes from the factor $(2x+1).$ This factor has a root of $x=-\frac{1}{2},$ and the exponent of the factor is $1.$ Therefore, the root $x=-\frac{1}{2}$ has multiplicity $1.$

In conclusion, there is no root with multiplicity $2.$
